challenge.method: Trace the specification's nested-call example. Challenge the interpretation that the enclosing call starts its function body before the calls in its argument list, or that every operand must evaluate.
challenge.results: The example invokes argument calls before the enclosing call and skips the conditional call when its left operand is true. The lexical rule governs eligible call events within the expression's evaluation dependencies. The example also leaves the timing of certain variable reads and indexing unspecified.

limitations: The direction applies to function-local evaluation and preserves call-argument dependencies. Some other operand evaluations have unspecified relative order, and short-circuiting can suppress calls.
